recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-13245 unless a future editorial change independently revises the Profiling page wording.
issue_request: FHIR-13245 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 technical correction for FHIR-core Profiling page section 5.1.0.13. It asked to repair the sentence "humans have understanding the implications of deep stacks of constraining profiles" so it instead says humans have trouble understanding those implications.
initial_application: Jira records application on Sept. 6, 2017. Git commit 7937711eec51f9228b8350291a074910a87c0adc, whose subject names GF #13245 among Profiling.html typo fixes, changed source/profiling.html from "humans have understanding" to "humans have trouble understanding".
additional_context: The current source/profiling.html file remains the FHIR-core Profiling narrative page referenced by the Jira related URL and already carries the corrected wording in the re-profiling section. The original Zulip bug-report thread listed the same profiling.html typo before the Jira task was filed. Confluence searches found no meeting record or page that conflicts with the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. An empty audit commit was published because source/profiling.html already says "humans have trouble understanding the implications of deep stacks of constraining profiles" and the combined branch did not already contain a FHIR-13245 reconcile commit.
